description: Data Scients (strateIA) in CDE, Paraguay.  Are Build bio-inspired edge AI (NVIDIA Jetson, Dual-Brain, VULGARIS) and AI for Scienco, an ISO 9001 clinical lab. We design zero-trust urban digital twins & Physarum traffic models with NASA data. Seeking UI/UX (3D/spatial), Earth Science/Urban experts & GIS/Data Analysts to build tangible climate resilience tools. Let's sync and build!
summary:
Hello, we are from Strateia, a team of data scientists. Gathering information from available NASA and ESA satellites helps us detect:
• River flood levels
• Fires and burning hotspots
• Rapid urban growth
• Access to healthcare and essential services
• Air turbidity (smoke, dust, and traffic emissions)
• Land surface heat and urban heat islands
• Water-laden clouds
• Traffic patterns
• Ground combustion
• Buildings and construction projects within the municipality
To solve these challenges, we implement Smart City Decision Intelligence to predict short-term disasters, respond to citizen needs, and improve quality of life, as well as address issues related to governance, access to public services, and industrial development.
details:
Dual Brain is our two-hemisphere architecture:

- a past hemisphere (memory and evidence: what happened, and from which source);

- a future hemisphere (proposal and simulation: what to do).

A "corpus callosum" connects the two, and the decision screen follows the same split. Everything runs on our own hardware: the interface and the analysis

run in the browser from local files (HTML, JavaScript, and bundled three.js, with no external loads), and the strateIA core is designed for an NVIDIA

Jetson AGX Orin edge server running open-weight models. City data never goes to the cloud.

Benefits

- Traceable decisions: every figure shows its source and confidence level: confirmed, suspected, or uncertain.

- Honesty: missing data is stated, never invented.

- Low cost and data sovereignty: open data, local hardware, and no cloud subscriptions.

- Speed: a 30-second guided walkthrough explains, in plain language, how the decision was reached.

Expected impact

- Help Ciudad del Este plan preventive relocation before floods.

- Locate persistent burning and prioritize roadworks.

- It can be replicated in other Latin American cities with the same open data.

Tools, languages, and hardware

- Code: Python (SQLite, data pipeline, pytest) and JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and SVG.

- Visualization: three.js 0.160.

- 3D model: Rhino 3D, driven through RhinoMCP, built from OpenStreetMap data.

- Quality: headless Chrome (Playwright) to verify every view, and gitleaks to detect secrets.

- Hardware: a Windows PC and a 64 GB NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin.

- AI assistance: Claude Code for development; AI-generated illustrations are labeled as such.

What makes it creative?

- Confidence levels instead of made-up percentages.

- The two-hemisphere metaphor (memory and proposal) as a way of reasoning.

- Satellites that point at real detections on the city model.

- A verification tag next to every figure: hover to see whether it is confirmed or suspected.

Factors we considered

- Data truthfulness: no figure without a source. Traffic data contributed by the team is labeled as not verified.

- Licensing: OpenStreetMap under ODbL; the public database excludes layers that cannot be redistributed.

- Privacy: no personal data.

- Human decision-making: AI supports, authorities decide.

- Offline operation.

- Accessibility: it respects reduced-motion preferences.

- Languages: Spanish and English.
